leak.narration.1: Hiss, hiss! There’s a tiny leak in one of our air modules.
leak.narration.2: Remember that quick patch? Sometimes a quick fix doesn’t hold.
leak.narration.3: Don’t worry, it’s a small one!
leak.dialogue.mei: I found it! We can patch it.
leak.dialogue.kai: Patching uses power. Backup oxygen is another way.
leak.question: How do we stop the leak?
leak.A.label: Patch the leak
leak.A.after: Patched! The air is staying inside now. It cost power, but the problem is solved.
leak.B.label: Use backup oxygen
leak.B.after: The backup tank keeps us breathing, but it won’t last forever, and the leak is still there.
leak.C.label: Everyone rests to use less air
leak.C.after: Resting saves air, but the crew can’t do science today. Slowing down is a real trick astronauts use.
leak.classroom: How did you protect the air supply?
meteors.narration.2: Mars has thin air, so more tiny meteors reach the ground than on Earth. Most are very small, but let’s check the roof.
meteors.dialogue.kai: Most are tiny, but a roof check never hurts.
meteors.question: What do we do?
meteors.A.label: Shelter the crew
meteors.A.after: Everyone stayed safe, and the roof is fine. We just lost a little research time.
meteors.B.label: Reinforce the roof
meteors.B.after: A stronger roof will protect us better from now on. It used some power today.
meteors.C.label: Keep going
meteors.C.after: We kept working, and a small piece hit a module. We lost a little air. A quick check could have helped.
meteors.classroom: What did you trade for protection?
minigame.patch_leak.hint: Tap each marked leak to place a patch. Patch all three, or choose Skip.
minigame.patch_leak.done: All three patches are fitted. You earned a small power bonus.
